newsitem.title: GABON: Gabon chooses second house of parliament.
newsitem.headline: Gabon chooses second house of parliament.

text.p: Gabon's municipal and regional councillors voted on Sunday to choose a 91-member senate, a new second house of parliament designed to promote a balance of power in the Central African oil-producing nation.
The elections, which end with a second round on February 9, are part of reforms launched after Gabon's political rivals struck a 1994 deal in Paris to defuse political unrest.
President Omar Bongo has ruled the former French colony since 1968 after the death of founding head of state, Leon Mba.

In 1990 Gabon, like other African nations, embarked on democratic reforms after the fall of Soviet-bloc communism but its democratic transition took a violent turn after Bongo's disputed election in 1993. Over a dozen people died in unrest.
The 1994 Paris Accords set the transition back on course.

Under the constitution, amended and approved by referendum in 1995, the national assembly and senate vote on all new laws. A joint commission will try to resolve any differences. In the event of deadlock, the national assembly takes precedence.
Bongo's supporters won 100 of the national assembly's 120 seats in December elections. The opposition fared better in October municipal polls, particularly in the capital.
A total of 2,043 councillors, elected in October, voted for senate members on Sunday in town halls around the country. Candidates included political party nominees and independents.
The senate elections, like the legislative and municipal elections before them, had been repeatedly delayed.
